description: We are a team of ambitious builders participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our mission is to build a real-world Earth science product using NASA data, software engineering, and scientific computing. We're looking for passionate problem-solvers with skills in software development, Python, AI/ML, data science, geospatial technologies, UI/UX, and research. We value curiosity, ownership, teamwork, and execution over titles. Let's build something meaningful.
summary:
THYRON is an evidence-first geospatial intelligence platform designed to support the investigation of landslide-dammed lakes and environmental hazards. It brings together satellite acquisition metadata, geospatial datasets, scientific processing workflows, and human-reviewed evidence in one integrated workspace.

The platform enables researchers to register data sources, inspect input quality, track processing parameters, preserve data provenance, and connect scientific observations to reviewable conclusions. It distinguishes verified observations and measurements from interpretations, hypotheses, and unresolved knowledge gaps.

THYRON aims to make complex geospatial investigations more transparent, reproducible, and accessible. By preserving the origin, processing history, and limitations of every result, it helps researchers and decision-makers evaluate evidence responsibly rather than relying on unsupported claims.
details:
RIVET — River Incident Verification & Evidence Twin

RIVET is an evidence-first geospatial intelligence platform developed to investigate the reported landslide-dammed lake along the Kuwari River in Bageshwar district, Uttarakhand, India.

The challenge is that satellite observations alone do not automatically establish whether a water body exists, how its boundaries change, or what is happening in a complex Himalayan river environment. Researchers need to understand the source, quality, processing history and limitations of every observation.

RIVET brings these capabilities together through an interactive spatial investigation map, a NASA NISAR acquisition registry, a scientific evidence ledger, processing-job management, human review and an auditable provenance system.

Our investigation examines the provisional NASA NISAR P05023 Group D40 acquisition pair from September 6 and September 30, 2026, using Frequency A, 40 MHz bandwidth and HH+HV polarization. The platform organizes acquisition metadata and supporting context from Sentinel-2, Landsat and Copernicus terrain data where available. It preserves distinctions between catalogue records, inspected metadata, retrieved assets and validated inputs.

The technical architecture combines Next.js, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL JS, Go, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and geospatial processing tools including GDAL and Rasterio.

RIVET's core innovation is its evidence-lineage approach. Scientific records can be traced through their source references, processing configurations, outputs and human-review decisions. This makes the investigation more transparent, reproducible and accountable.

The intended impact is to support researchers and environmental decision-makers in evaluating Himalayan river and landslide-dam evidence more responsibly.

RIVET does not claim a confirmed lake boundary, validated water detection or breach prediction. It explicitly preserves scientific uncertainty and identifies unresolved data gaps.

Super Intelligence Disclosure

ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex were used as development assistants for software planning, code-generation assistance, debugging, technical explanations and documentation. AI-generated suggestions were subject to human review and software testing. AI tools were not treated as primary satellite data sources or as independent scientific validation authorities. The project team remains responsible for the accuracy of its scientific interpretations and submitted results.
